author: Gabriela Blanchard For the Herald
title: Michelle's Sweet Creations moves to Fair Haven | Local News | rutlandherald.com
text:
FAIR HAVEN — After seven years of serving freshly baked sweet treats in Castleton, Michelle Scott has moved her bakery, Michelle’s Sweet Creations, to 73 Main St.
With the new location’s large, sunny windows shining a bright light on her new endeavor, the little girl who started baking with her grandma said she is beyond proud.
“I have always dreamed of having a large bakery with seating for customers to relax and enjoy their sweets,” Scott said.
What started as the former owner of Old School Bagels asking Scott if she wanted to buy a dough sheeter turned into a conversation that led to the closing of her Castleton location, followed by a soft opening of the Fair Haven shop on Aug. 15.
“We had kind of outgrown it a million times over there in the last year or so,” Scott said. “But this just kind of happened, I wasn’t really looking, just had it in the back of my mind if I could find a space that was big enough.”
As for the actual move, Scott said it was very overwhelming; however, with help from her kids and fiancé, she got it done in just a couple of weeks, so she could reopen as soon as possible.
“It was amazing all the stuff we moved and how much I had crammed into the little bakery,” Scott said.
Scott’s new Fair Haven space was previously home to Old School Bagels, which she bought from owner Bob Workman. She is now renting the building for the two businesses to grow as Michelle’s Sweet Creations & Old School Bagels Bakery & Cafe.
Scott has incorporated the bagel shop’s menu into her new menu, an addition her regulars have approved.
“I like the bread of the sandwich, a breakfast sandwich on a bagel,” Roger Louiselle said. “I know she has other things you can put it on, too, but I had a breakfast sandwich on a bagel, and I really liked it.”
Scott said she’s slowly working on the menu.
“I kind of left what they had before, just changed a couple things. I kind of wanted to get a feel for what everybody’s looking for first,” she said, adding she’s starting to bring in soups, macaroni and cheese and salads.
Although some patrons were disappointed when first hearing about the move, they said they now see the great opportunities the new space offers.
“I was disappointed when hearing about the move — Michelle’s was a great addition for Castleton, and I often stopped there after stopping at the diner,” frequent customer John Ragosta said. “But, if this allows Michelle to do a lunch business, that is good, and Fair Haven definitely needed a good lunch place.”
Similarly, Louiselle said he would travel from Rutland over to Castleton just to buy Scott’s baked goods, saying it’s well worth the trip.
“Another five miles down the road for me is nothing,” Louiselle said. Every time we drive through Castleton, if she’s open, we stop. As for special trips, I would say we go two, three times a month. But then if I’m just driving through, I automatically stop.”
Scott said the best part about the new location is the seating space that the old location couldn’t offer, unless it was outside.
However, even good changes aren’t without some challenges. Scott said the biggest one has probably been trying to figure out how to manage and make sure she has enough people on staff at once.
“Especially as the lines at the cash register and out the door have been a lot some days,” Scott said. “But it’s going well, and we’re adjusting.”
As long-time customers have visited the new location, they said they are happy to still see their favorite items have returned.
Louiselle particularly raves about the scones. He said Scott’s are the best ones he has ever had — the maple and blueberry flavors being his favorite.
“Not only do they look great, but they are huge and so, so good,” Louiselle said. “And the good thing is, sometimes you get scones that’ve only got a little bit of filling in it, but not Michelle’s. It’s like she scooped them in with a tablespoon.”
Scott said she is happy to finally be building her lifelong dream. She said seeing all her new customers while also having her regulars from Castleton still visiting her, has been an absolute dream come true.
“I was absolutely blown away by all the love and support when we moved here, and how busy we were — that has been absolutely wonderful.”
